title: How to Structure a Lipstick Development Brief
summary: Define finish, shade architecture, payoff, wear, packaging and price position before the first sample round.
intro: A useful lipstick brief connects the product experience to a clear consumer, channel and commercial target.
sections: Define the hero shade, supporting shades, target consumer, channel and price position.
Describe finish, payoff, glide, wear, fragrance and care expectations, supported by reference samples where possible.
Shade, bullet integrity, fill, component fit, decoration and label content form one finished system.
content: Build a lipstick brief around commercial goals, sensorial direction, shade architecture and finished-pack approval.

title: Choosing the Right Sunscreen Format
summary: Compare spray, gel, cream, lotion and stick formats by use occasion, texture, packaging and testing needs.
intro: The best format follows application behavior, target market and the evidence required for the final claim set.
sections: Daily face wear, body application, sport and travel formats create different texture and packaging needs.
Spreadability, residue, glide, spray pattern, dose and component compatibility should be part of the brief.
SPF, broad-spectrum and water-resistance claims require finished-formula testing and market review.
content: Choose a sunscreen format by application experience, packaging system, target claims and validation plan.

title: From Inquiry to Production: The OEM/ODM Decision Path
summary: A practical view of qualification, sampling, quotation, approval and production handoffs.
intro: Projects move faster when commercial, product, quality and packaging decisions have a visible owner and next action.
sections: Confirm market, channel, quantity, target price, launch date and decision criteria.
Align formula, shade or texture, components, decoration and required evidence.
Quotation, testing, labels, quality checkpoints and delivery terms should match the approved finished product.
content: Manage an OEM/ODM project through clear qualification, sampling, quotation, approval and production stages.
